guides.compress-wedding-photos.title: Compress Wedding Photos Without Losing Print Quality
guides.compress-wedding-photos.desc: How to shrink wedding photo files for sharing and web upload while keeping a print-quality archive, with practical JPEG and WebP settings.
guides.compress-wedding-photos.lead: Keep two versions: the original files untouched for print, and a compressed set for sharing. Compressing the only copy is the mistake to avoid.
guides.compress-wedding-photos.f2v: Often 25–35% smaller than JPEG at similar quality
guides.compress-wedding-photos.f3v: Keep originals in a separate folder, never overwritten
guides.compress-wedding-photos.f4v: Strip GPS before public sharing if privacy matters
guides.compress-wedding-photos.s1: Compression works by discarding detail the eye is least likely to notice, so repeated saves degrade an image each time. Always start from the original, export once at your chosen quality, and never re-save a JPEG on top of itself. For a sharing set, resizing the long edge to 2000–2500 pixels usually saves more bytes than any quality tweak.
guides.compress-wedding-photos.s2: File-size limits differ by channel: email attachments are often capped around 20–25 MB, messaging apps recompress aggressively, and many wedding upload portals set a per-file ceiling. If you are sending photos to guests internationally, a download link beats an attachment. Note that some printing labs reject WebP, so keep a JPEG export for print orders even if you use WebP on the web.
guides.compress-wedding-photos.s3: Do not compress before you have backed up the originals, and do not strip all metadata from your archive — EXIF dates are how you reconstruct the day's order. Strip location data only from the copies you share publicly. Watch for banding in skies and smooth gradients, which is where aggressive JPEG compression shows first.
guides.compress-wedding-photos.q1: What JPEG quality should I use?
guides.compress-wedding-photos.a1: 80–85 for sharing is a good balance. For anything headed to print, export at 90–95 or keep the original.
guides.compress-wedding-photos.q2: Does resizing matter more than quality?
guides.compress-wedding-photos.a2: Usually yes. Reducing a 6000 px photo to 2400 px cuts file size far more than dropping quality from 95 to 80.
guides.compress-wedding-photos.a3: Many labs only accept JPEG or TIFF. Use WebP on the web, but keep a JPEG export for anything you intend to print.
